subject: BridgePoint: sudden throughput spike and errors — KV prefetch misalignment
messages:
From: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@bridgepoint.com>
To: support@redwood.ai, dylan_brooks@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: High error rate + throughput drop in prod (region us-west)

Hi team,

We're seeing a sudden jump in latency and errors across our `/generate` route—p50 is up ~3x and p99 is spiking. Throughput is also unstable: we have intermittent drops to ~20% of normal TPS and a correlating surge in 429/500 responses. This started ~08:40 PT.

Attached a small set of error logs and a screenshot of our dashboard. We need immediate help — this is impacting a live demo at 11:00 PT.

What we know:
- All traffic is routed to the us-west cluster.
- We haven't changed model or config from our side.
- A subset of requests show long tail behind a batching wait (timeouts in worker logs).

Please escalate as needed.

Thanks,
Sarah Liu\Client Success Manager\BridgePoint

Attachments: bridgepoint-error-sample.log, screenshot-ratechart.png

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
CC: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop in prod (region us-west)

Looping in ops/infra owners. Initial triage notes:
- Observed HOL blocking on several GPU lanes in us-west-2 cluster starting 08:38 PT. Backing traces show a small number of large KV prefix misses causing long tail token decoding times; while waiting the batching window held up lanes and created head-of-line stalls.
- Autoscaling still healthy; not a capacity shortage but a batching + KV prefetch misalignment.

Immediate mitigation I'm deploying now:
1) Reduce max batching window from 30ms -> 10ms for the affected route to reduce HOL blocking.
2) Temporarily increase KV prefetch concurrency to avoid single-request prefix misses blocking lanes.
3) Add a short-lived route-level bypass that disables prefix caching for requests flagged as long-prompts (we'll revert after stabilization).

I'll post changes and watch p99/p50, error rates. Markus, can you validate the prefetch concurrency change won't regress small-prompt latency?

Evelyn
SRE Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop in prod (region us-west)

Thanks — confirmed. The prefetch concurrency knob was set conservatively after the last throughput regression; it looks like BridgePoint's traffic included a micro-burst of long-context requests which caused a flurry of cache misses. Two compounding issues:

- Prefetch window aligns poorly with batching lanes: when a long-request misses the KV, its worker waits for prefetch and holds the batch slot (HOL).
- Our fairness heuristic underestimated skewed tenant workloads — BridgePoint's traffic pattern temporarily pinned several hot shards.

I've pushed the concurrency bump and adjusted the prefetch TTL for prefix entries from 60s -> 120s to reduce churn. Monitoring now.

Also created a short runbook note under the incident doc: "prefetch-misalignment -> reduce batching window; increase prefetch concurrency; protect hot shards with tenant-priority split."

-Markus
Staff Eng, Inference Runtime

Attachments: p99-traces-20280530.zip
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Liu <sarah.liu@bridgepoint.com>, ops@bridgepoint.com
Cc: evelyn_hart@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: High error rate + throughput drop in prod (region us-west)

Sarah — quick update: engineering pushed three mitigations (reduced batch window, increased prefetch concurrency, extended prefix TTL). We're seeing errors drop back toward baseline and p99 coming down. Attaching a quick summary and the runbook entry.

Next steps we propose:
- Short-term (this afternoon): keep the temporary bypass for long-prompts for 4 hours while we monitor.
- Near-term (3–5 days): A config tweak to split BridgePoint's traffic onto a separate priority lane to prevent hot-shard contamination.
- Follow-up: we'll schedule a post-mortem with you and provide recommended config defaults and a tailored caching profile.

Can we get sign-off to keep the bypass active for up to 4 hours? We want to avoid flipping it off while we monitor.

Thanks for the quick heads-up and sample logs — they helped narrow this down fast.

—Dylan
